ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, a unit lattice can be seen, with points arranged at equal intervals in the horizontal and vertical directions; thick black lines connect several lattice points to form a polygon. Taking the lower-left point as (0,0), rightward as the positive x direction, and upward as the positive y direction, then reading the polygon vertices in order along the boundary from the image gives (0,2) → (1,2) → (2,3) → (2,2) → (3,2) → (3,0) → (2,0) → (2,1) → (1,0) → (0,0) → back to (0,2). Use the shoelace formula to calculate the area. The forward cross sum is 0·2 + 1·3 + 2·2 + 2·2 + 3·0 + 3·0 + 2·1 + 2·0 + 1·0 + 0·2 = 13. The reverse cross sum is 2·1 + 2·2 + 3·2 + 2·3 + 2·3 + 0·2 + 0·2 + 1·1 + 0·0 + 0·0 = 25. Area = |13 - 25| / 2 = 6.
